newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deficits continue during restructure-Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deficits continue during restructure-Malan.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said public sector accounts were on the mend, but operational and trade balance deficits would continue so long as the economy was restructuring.
"We are moving in the right direction in terms of public sector accounts," Malan told businessmen at a seminar on economic development at the National Development Bank (BNDES).

Malan said the operational public sector deficit fell to 3.4 percent of gross domestic product over the past 12 months from 3.9 percent in 1996 and forecast it would drop to below three percent for all of 1997.
Malan said the deficits in the trade and current account deficits were a natural part of the transformation which the Brazilian economy was undergoing.
He stressed however, they were being increasingly financed by direct investment and not just "hot money."
"As long as the restructuring of the economy continues, there will be a deficit in the trade balance and the current account," Malan said.

He said 42 percent of the current account deficit was being financed by foreign direct investment (FDI), which he said had totalled $12 billion over the past 12 months. FDI for all of 1996 was of $9.4 billion.
Malan said the way to address the current account deficit was to increase private savings and diminish the public sector debt.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 507 4151))
